topic.readerProblem: A reader searching what answer engine optimization is, or whether AIO, LLMO, LLM SEO and SEO for LLMs mean something different, wants one clear definition, a straight answer on the labels, and what to actually do so AI engines name their brand.
topic.connection: AEO is AEOeye's core subject: the page defines it, explains how AI engines retrieve and choose brands, and shows how to measure whether engines recommend a brand, using AEOeye's own crawler access study and recommendation benchmark with their caveats.

assessment: Consolidates five overlapping AEOeye pages (AEO definition, AI optimization, LLM optimization, LLM SEO, SEO for LLMs) into one answer-first guide: a single terminology table, a three-layer program (retrievable, quotable, corroborated) plus measurement, and a what-doesn't-work section. It rests on Google's own AI-search guidance, the GEO and earned-media papers, Pew and SparkToro data, vendor crawler documentation, and AEOeye's crawler access study and recommendation benchmark, each with its limits stated. It deliberately does not claim any tactic guarantees citations, drops the unsourced statistics and the Princeton backlink claim carried by the earlier pages, does not repeat the unverified AEO voice-search lineage, and does not present per-engine benchmark rates as comparisons.

sources.supports: Google guide (last updated 2026-07-10): optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO; pages must be indexed; RAG and query fan-out description; no special files, markup, chunking or writing style needed; inauthentic mentions help less than they seem; Google Search does not use llms.txt; Generative AI performance report in Search Console; names AEO and GEO.

GEO paper (KDD 2024): 10K-query GEO-bench; citations, quotations and statistics gave 30-40% relative gains on Position-Adjusted Word Count; keyword stuffing little to no improvement and about 10% worse than baseline on Perplexity.ai; effects vary by domain; GPT-3.5 and Perplexity.ai setups.

Chen et al. 2025: AI search shows a systematic bias toward earned media over brand-owned and social content; software test earned share 74.2% (Canada) and 72.7% (US) for gpt-4o-search-preview versus 31.8% and 45.4% for Google top ten; AI search services differ in domain diversity and freshness.
Pew Research Center: 900 US adults, March 2025; clicked a traditional result in 8% of visits with an AI summary versus 15% without, and a link inside the summary in 1%.
SparkToro: 2,961 runs, November-December 2025; under a 1-in-100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI repeats the same brand list; advice to ask at least 60-100 times.

OpenAI crawler documentation: OAI-SearchBot is for ChatGPT search and opted-out sites will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers; GPTBot is for training; robots.txt updates take about 24 hours to take effect; llms.txt appears only as the docs index link.
Anthropic help article (updated 2026-04-07): ClaudeBot is for training, Claude-SearchBot is for search quality, Claude-User is user-directed; the page does not mention llms.txt.
Perplexity crawler documentation: PerplexityBot surfaces and links sites in Perplexity search and is not used for foundation-model training; llms.txt appears only as the docs index link.

Wikipedia (edited 2026-10-01): GEO is also known as AEO and AIO; related names include LLMO and AI SEO; usage varies with no consensus definition; the term GEO was introduced in a 2023 paper presented at KDD 2024.
Wikipedia (edited 2026-09-28): RAG lets LLMs retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources; combines a parametric model with retrieval at inference time.
Microsoft Advertising blog by a Bing Principal Product Manager, 2025-10-08: GEO, AIO and SEO used interchangeably; crawlability, metadata and internal linking remain the SEO baseline.
Google spam policies (updated 2026-08-28): scaled content abuse includes using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value for users.
llms.txt proposal by Jeremy Howard: a Markdown file at /llms.txt with curated links to give LLM-friendly content.
Vercel analysis published 2024-12-17: major AI crawlers including OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot did not render JavaScript; recommendation to server-render critical content.
Hugging Face guide to optimizing LLMs for speed and memory: lower-precision quantization, Flash Attention and architectural changes; shows the engineering meaning of LLM optimization.
Search Engine Journal (2025-04-01) uses AIO as shorthand for Google's AI Overviews, supporting the claim that some SEOs mean AI Overviews by AIO.
